models_evaluated: Bayesian network fall-risk prediction model (AI-powered CDS)

links.outcome: Fall-prediction performance variation across 4 hospital sites
links.effect: Locally optimized models across 4 sites had AUROCs of 0.8051-0.9581 without heuristic tools (0.9309-0.9851 with), described as little performance variation.
links.quote: The 4 hospitals successfully implemented prediction models with little performance variation; the AUROCs were 0.8051-0.9581.

links.outcome: Mapping of model input constructs to local EMR data elements
links.effect: Only 4 of 6 concept-model constructs mapped to local data; KPCS data unavailable at site D; medication mapped to local drug classes; local statements covered 48.0%-86.7%.
links.quote: Four of the 6 constructs in the concept model were successfully mapped to local data elements.

links.outcome: AI model discrimination versus existing heuristic fall-risk tools
links.effect: AI models AUROC 0.8051-0.9851 versus heuristic tools alone AUROC 0.6491-0.7364.
links.quote: For both of these the performance was better than for the heuristic tools alone (AUROC = 0.6491–0.7364).

links.outcome: Longitudinal inpatient fall rate after enterprise CDS deployment
links.effect: No significant fall-rate decrease: -0.50 per 1000 hospital-days (P = .160, CI -1.21 to 0.21); nursing interventions increased.
links.quote: There was no significant longitudinal decrease in the fall rate (P = .160, 95% CI = -1.21 to 0.21 per 1000 hospital days), but rates of interventions provided by nurses were notably increased.

unlisted_practices: Using standardized nursing terminologies (ICNP, LOINC) to map AI model inputs and CDS content across heterogeneous EMR systems

openai.sample_unit: hospital admissions in the four retrospective modeling cohorts
models_evaluated: Bayesian-network fall-risk prediction model, locally optimized at four hospitals

links.outcome: Predictive discrimination compared with conventional fall-risk assessment tools
links.effect: AI-model AUROCs were 0.9309–0.9851 with heuristic-tool inputs and 0.8051–0.9581 without them, versus 0.6491–0.7364 for heuristic tools alone.
links.quote: For both of these the performance was better than for the heuristic tools alone (AUROC = 0.6491–0.7364).

links.outcome: Variation in predictive performance across locally optimized hospital implementations
links.effect: Around 15% synchronic variation was reported; AUROCs without heuristic-tool inputs were 0.8051, 0.8740, 0.9334, and 0.9581 at sites A–D, respectively.
links.quote: We optimized the concept model for each site and found around 15% synchronic variation among the models.

links.outcome: Change in inpatient fall rates following CDS deployment
links.effect: No significant fall-rate improvement: immediate change −0.50 per 1000 hospital-days (P = .160, CI = −1.21 to 0.21); monthly trend change − 0.03 (P = .354, CI = −0.10 to 0.04).
links.quote: In the first month after CDS tool deployment, a −0.50 decrease was observed in the fall rate ( P = .160, CI = −1.21 to 0.21), followed by a − 0.03 decrease in the monthly trend ( P = .354, CI = −0.10 to 0.04).

unlisted_practices: Use standardized nursing terminologies and a guideline-based fall-prevention catalog to harmonize local EHR inputs, care-plan statements, and outcome tracking across hospitals.

models_evaluated: Locally optimized Bayesian network models for fall risk

links.outcome: longitudinal fall rates and nurse interventions
links.effect: no significant fall rate decrease (-1.21 to 0.21) but intervention rates increased
links.quote: There was no significant longitudinal decrease in the fall rate (P = .160, 95% CI = -1.21 to 0.21 per 1000 hospital days), but rates of interventions provided by nurses were notably increased.
